title: Checks — steel EN 1993, timber and CLT EN 1995, concrete EN 1992, free material on stress
emptyHint: Click "Run checks" — the model is solved first if needed, then steel, timber, CLT, concrete and the stress check run together in one go.
noCheckable: No checkable members: no steel profiles (HEA/HEB/IPE/…), timber grades (C24, GL28h, …), CLT layup, concrete class or free material in the model.
solverFailed: Solving failed — check the model (supports, loads).
timberFiltered: {{count}} timber result(s) not included in the PDF — the PDF report currently covers steel (EN 1993) only.
runFirst: Run the code checks first (Check tab) before generating a PDF.

cfg.bucklingHint: Empty = the calculation core chooses and states the origin in the check: the member length, or about z the distance between lateral restraints at both the top and the bottom flange.
cfg.bucklingOutOfPlaneHint: The frame analysis never sees out-of-plane buckling, not even second order: the buckling check about z is always required. A lateral restraint only shortens L_cr,z where the top and bottom flange are restrained at the same position.
cfg.herkomstKipsteunen: from restraints at top and bottom flange
cfg.bracingTimberHint: For timber only used for L_cr,z: a position counts as a support where both the top and the bottom edge are restrained. The lateral torsional check uses the restraint spacing.
cfg.bracingHint: Fractions of the member length (0–1), separated by commas or spaces — e.g. "0.5" or "0.25 0.5 0.75". Empty = no restraints.
cfg.deflClassHint: Categories from NEN-EN 1990:2002/NB:2019 A1.4.3(3) for the additional deflection w_add.
cfg.deflCustomTimberHint: For timber, L/n applies to both w_fin and w_add.
cfg.deflAddNumeratorHint: Overrides the numerator that belongs to the class and applies to the member length. Only fill this in to reproduce an external reference calculation with a fixed numerator (e.g. L/150); the report then states that the numerator was supplied.
cfg.preCamberHint: Pre-camber in mm, positive = upward (against a sagging beam). Only for a mainly horizontal member; for a member at 75° or more no pre-camber is taken into account. Not included in w_add.
cfg.durHint: Automatic: k_mod follows, per ULS combination, from the load with the shortest duration (EN 1995-1-1 3.1.3(2)). A chosen class acts as a lower bound: it can only lengthen the duration.
cfg.timberHint: Determines k_mod and k_def in the EN 1995 checks.
cfg.staleResultHint: The shown result is from an earlier run with a different material type — run the checks again.
cfg.sprongLiggendFlens: Note: this member leans to the left at {{helling}}, {{afstand}} below the {{grens}} limit above which a member counts as upright. Top is currently the physical upper side (upper right). From {{grens}} on, top becomes the left side — at this inclination the physical underside (lower left). A small change to the nodes then silently flips which side these restraints are on.
cfg.sprongStaandFlens: Note: this member leans to the left at {{helling}}, {{afstand}} above the {{grens}} limit. Top is the left side here, which at this inclination is the physical UNDERSIDE (lower left) — not the upper face. Below {{grens}}, top would be the physical upper side. After changing the nodes, check which side these restraints are on.
cfg.sprongLiggendKorf: Note: this member leans to the left at {{helling}}, {{afstand}} below the {{grens}} limit above which a member counts as upright. The top reinforcement is currently on the physical upper side (upper right). From {{grens}} on, it is on the left side — at this inclination the physical underside (lower left). A small change to the nodes then silently flips which side the top and bottom reinforcement are on.
cfg.sprongStaandKorf: Note: this member leans to the left at {{helling}}, {{afstand}} above the {{grens}} limit. The top reinforcement is on the left side here, which at this inclination is the physical UNDERSIDE (lower left) — not the upper face. Below {{grens}}, it would be on the physical upper side. After changing the nodes, check which side the top and bottom reinforcement are on.
cfg.bucklingHintTimber: For timber, L_cr,z also enters the compression term of the lateral-torsional buckling check (6.35).
cfg.ltbSupportSpacingHint: Lateral restraint spacing empty = member length. This is the ℓ from which table 6.1 derives the effective length l_ef; l_ef governs σ_m,crit and therefore k_crit (6.33)/(6.35).
cfg.performLtbCheckOffHint: Lateral-torsional buckling check off: you declare that the compression edge is laterally restrained over its full length (roof sheathing, floor deck) and that the supports are torsionally restrained, so k_crit = 1.0 (art. 6.3.3(5)). This assumption is stated as such in the report.
cfg.kCrHint: b_ef = k_cr · b (6.13a). Empty = 1.0: NEN-EN 1995-1-1/NB at 6.1.7 for a prismatic cross-section. The European recommendation of 6.1.7(2) is 0.67 for sawn timber and glulam; only values in (0, 1] are stored.
cfg.cltKdefHint: Table 3.2 of EN 1995-1-1 gives no k_def for cross-laminated timber, and the national annex adds none. No value is therefore assumed: enter k_def and its source (ETA or product declaration of the panel, for this service class). If either is missing, w_fin and w_add are not checked and that reason is stated in the report.

properties.title: Properties
properties.relPrincipal: relative to principal axes u, v
properties.perimeterAssembly: An assembly is a sum of plates that overlap at the welds; there is no unique outer boundary.
properties.shapeFactorYTitle: W_pl/W_el: how much the cross-section still contributes once yielding has started. Rectangle 1.5; rolled I about the strong axis about 1.13.
properties.welUVTitle: Governing of both extreme fibres. u: {{uPlus}} / {{uMin}} · v: {{vPlus}} / {{vMin}} mm³
properties.plasticCentroidTitle: The line that divides the area in two halves. For a symmetric cross-section it coincides with the elastic centroid; for a T-section it lies higher.
properties.zjTitle: z_j = z_s − ½·∬(y²+z²)z dA / I_y, the monosymmetry term of the lateral-torsional buckling check. Zero for a doubly symmetric cross-section; positive when most material lies above the centroid.
properties.yjTitle: The mirror image of z_j; governing for a channel section.
properties.betaTitle: The monosymmetry constants from which z_j and y_j follow: z_j = −β_y/2.
properties.staticMomentsTitle: ∬z dA and ∬y dA about the axes of the input coordinate system. About the centroidal axes they are zero by definition, so Q_y = A·z_c is a direct check on the calculation.
properties.itThinWalledTitle: Thin-walled: ⅓·Σb·t³ plus Bredt for declared cells

main.moveTargetPoint: Move ({{wat}}) · 2/2 target point: Δy = {{dy}} mm, Δz = {{dz}} mm

main.noHoleYet: There is no hole to edit yet: add one on the left.

main.holeAnchorExplain: Mirroring is about the vertical centreline of the section. Otherwise a hole stays in its own plate: moving slides it along that plate, rotating shifts a hole in the tube wall along the circumference and turns a rectangular slotted hole with it.
main.holeRotateAbout: each hole follows its own position — a hole in the tube wall slides along the circumference, a rectangular slotted hole turns with it, and whatever is not possible is reported in the bar
main.holeMirrorAbout: the vertical centreline of the section

main.blockTargetAll: Target: all {{n}} building blocks. Click a building block in the drawing or in the list to edit only that one.
main.blockAnchorExplain: Rotating and mirroring are about {{om}}. A single selected building block rotates about its own centre; the whole design rotates about the centroid from the engine — or about the origin as long as the engine has not returned anything yet.

canvas.empty: Nothing drawn yet. Choose a starting shape on the left or add a plate.
canvas.gridInfo: grid {{stap}} mm · snaps to points and grid (Shift = free)

stress.forcesTitle: Internal forces on this cross-section. Tension positive; positive M_y gives tension in the bottom fibre. The distribution is calculated with this single set — no member, no combinations, only the cross-section.
stress.nTitle: Axial force N_Ed; tension positive. Gives σ = N/A over the whole cross-section.
stress.vzTitle: Shear force V_z,Ed. Determines τ = V·S(z)/(I_y·b(z)) and the shear flow through the welds.
stress.myTitle: Moment M_y,Ed about the strong axis; positive gives tension in the bottom fibre.
stress.sigmaZTitle: Transverse stress, assumed constant over the cross-section — for example a bearing pressure. A member model does not calculate it by itself.
stress.materialTitle: This is the FREE stress check: no cross-section classification, no local buckling, no buckling or lateral-torsional buckling. You enter the allowable stress yourself; f_d = f_toel/γ_M is the dashed line in the σ_eq panel.
stress.fAllowTitle: Allowable stress. For steel usually f_y.
stress.gammaMTitle: Material factor; f_d = f_toel/γ_M. 1.0 makes f_toel itself the design value.
stress.steelTitle: Steel grade of the weakest connected part — this gives f_u (EN 1993-1-1 table 3.1) and the correlation factor β_w (EN 1993-1-8 table 4.1) for the weld check.
stress.noDistribution: No stress distribution: see the message on the left.
stress.enterForces: Enter a moment or a shear force on the left.
stress.stripsTitle: How many horizontal strips the cross-section is built from; A, z_c, I_y and S(z) follow from those strips.
stress.deviationTitle: Difference between the strip model behind this distribution and the exact contour of the section engine. For plain plates this should be zero; a catalogue part is included as straight plates, so the root fillet shows up here.
stress.weldsTitle: Per weld the shear flow q = V_z·S/I_y and the check according to NEN-EN 1993-1-8 4.5.3.3 (simplified method).

assembly.plateHelp: Rectangular plate. The position is the centroid of the plate, b is the dimension along the plate and t the thickness; α = 0 is horizontal, α = 90 vertical. Dragging in the drawing area moves a plate.
assembly.partHelp: A catalogue section as a building block, placed at the centroid of that part. Note: with catalogue parts W_pl is not determined and the cross-section goes to the check as properties — not as geometry.
assembly.cellIncluded_one: Closed cell recognised from {{count}} plate; the torsional stiffness is included using Bredt's formula. Clear the checkbox to use only the open formula ⅓·Σb·t³.
assembly.cellIncluded_other: Closed cell recognised from {{count}} plates; the torsional stiffness is included using Bredt's formula. Clear the checkbox to use only the open formula ⅓·Σb·t³.
assembly.cellExcluded_one: Closed cell recognised from {{count}} plate, but it is not included: I_t is determined with the open formula ⅓·Σb·t³ and then strongly underestimates the box section.
assembly.cellExcluded_other: Closed cell recognised from {{count}} plates, but it is not included: I_t is determined with the open formula ⅓·Σb·t³ and then strongly underestimates the box section.
assembly.cellNone: No closed cell recognised: the plates do not form a single ring, so the cross-section is open. The checkbox then has no effect.
assembly.presetsTitle: A starting shape replaces the current assembly with a ready-made set of building blocks.
assembly.blocksTitle: Everything the cross-section is built from. Click a building block to select it; the toolbar then edits only that one.
assembly.empty: Choose a starting shape above, or add a building block.
assembly.plateYTitle: Centroid of the plate, to the right
assembly.partYTitle: Centroid of the part, to the right
assembly.partAlphaTitle: Rotation of the part, counter-clockwise positive
assembly.mirroredTitle: Mirrors the part about its own vertical axis (y → −y), for example for two channel sections back to back.

holes.help: A hole through a plate leaves a gap over the full plate thickness in the cross-section plane: the net cross-section at the hole. A web hole splits the cross-section into two tees — I_w then drops out and I_t adds up.
holes.dimensionsTitle: Overall dimensions and wall thicknesses of the chosen catalogue section.
holes.empty: No holes yet — add one above.

welds.help: A weld in a cross-section is a longitudinal weld: it runs along the member and transfers the shear flow q = V·S/I_y between the plates. So there is no weld length — the length is the member length. What the weld has to resist is shown on the Stress tab. The weld material is NOT included in A, I_y and the other section properties: the section engine calculates with the plates, as is usual for a welded cross-section.
welds.noPlatesTitle: There are not yet two plates to place a weld between.
welds.allWeldedTitle: Every seam between two touching plates already has a weld.
welds.addTitle_one: Place a weld on the first free seam ({{count}} available). {{help}}
welds.addTitle_other: Place a weld on the first free seam ({{count}} available). {{help}}
welds.oneFreeTitle: There is at most one free seam; use ＋ Weld.
welds.allTitle: Place a double-sided fillet weld on all {{n}} free seams.
welds.emptyNoPlates: Two plates that touch each other have a seam; place a weld there.
welds.emptyNoTouch: No two plates touch each other, so there is no seam.
welds.typeTitle: Double-sided: a fillet weld on both sides of the plate — two throat sections. Single-sided: one. Full penetration butt weld: NEN-EN 1993-1-8 4.7.1 gives the weld the resistance of the weakest connected part, so no separate weld check.
welds.throatTitle: Throat thickness of one weld. NEN-EN 1993-1-8 4.5.2(2): not less than 3 mm.

toolbar.moveTitle: Move in two clicks: first the base point you pick up, then the target point where it should go. toolbar.dyTitle: Displacement to the right, in millimetres. Negative is to the left.

toolbar.applyMoveTitle: Move the target by Δy and Δz
toolbar.applyMoveInvalid: First enter a non-zero Δy or Δz

variants.compareHint: Checks the same member again with the next section up and down — resistance only, with the same force distribution.
variants.noCurrentResult: no check result for the current cross-section
variants.title: Neighbouring cross-sections
variants.determinateNote: The variants below only recheck the resistance; that is correct here.
variants.indeterminateNote: The variants below recheck ONLY the resistance. The actual unity check of a variant differs from this; the “Deviation” column states per row in which direction.
variants.footer: Click a row to see the full derivation of that variant.

cage.noExposureClassHint: Without an exposure class the concrete cover is not checked against the code. Table 4.1 of NEN-EN 1992-1-1 describes the classes; 4.4.1.2 derives the minimum cover from them.
cage.perSideHintAfter: concrete surface, i.e. per side. Empty = that side follows the exposure class and cover of the element above; nothing is assumed. The top face governs the position of the top reinforcement (d₂), the bottom face that of the bottom reinforcement (d), and the side faces the transverse spacing of the stirrup legs (§9.2.2(8)) and the clear bar spacing (§8.2). Left and right are not separate: they only ever appear as a pair in each formula (b_w − 2c), so splitting them would not change any number — if their environments really differ, use the more severe one. The structural class remains one for the whole element: all five criteria of table 4.3N as replaced by the national annex are properties of the element.
cage.noShearCheck: Without stirrup spacing s and number of legs n the shear check cannot run.
cage.undeterminedB: from (9.4) are then undetermined. The code gives no default value here — §9.2.2(6) and (8) only give upper limits — so nothing is assumed.
cage.stirrupAngleHint: The stirrup angle α is fixed at 90° (vertical stirrups); §9.2.2(1) allows 45°–90°, but inclined stirrups and bent-up bars are not modelled.
cage.stDerived: for this two-leg stirrup s_t = {{st}} mm follows from b_w, cover and stirrup diameter.
cage.stDerivedByEngine: for a two-leg stirrup the engine derives it geometrically from b_w, cover and stirrup diameter; with more legs §9.2.2(8) remains unchecked.
cage.fywkEmpty: left empty means: the same steel grade as the longitudinal reinforcement.
cage.sideBarsHint: , between the corner bars. They are distributed evenly between the bottom and top rows — a modelling choice, not a code requirement; §9.5.3(6) only limits the distance to a restrained bar to 150 mm.
cage.noSideBarsHint: Only for a column. 0 = no side bars; the corner bars belong to the top and bottom rows, not here.
cage.coverTooSmall: Cover too small at the {{zijde}}: {{aanwezig}} mm while {{vereist}} mm is required
cage.coverOk: Cover OK; governing is the {{zijde}}: {{aanwezig}} mm ≥ {{vereist}} mm.
cage.coverOkAllSides: Cover OK on all sides; governing is the {{zijde}}: {{aanwezig}} mm ≥ {{vereist}} mm.
cage.coverCheckFailed: The cover check could not run ({{fout}}). The cover has therefore not been checked against the exposure class.

cageEditor.effectiveWidthHintA: The flange width should be the EFFECTIVE width b
cageEditor.effectiveWidthHintB: — 5.3.2.1(3), equation (5.7). When checking the model, the calculation engine derives it from the beam line and replaces the value entered here; the result always states the width used.
cageEditor.ellHint: In this uniaxial model an L is calculated exactly like a T; this only holds if lateral bending is prevented, for example by a floor diaphragm. That assumption is stated in every result.
cageEditor.stripsHint: Into how many parts the cross-section is divided for integrating the concrete stress. The error decreases quadratically; with 50 strips it is below 0.05 %.

cagePanel.noEquilibriumAxial: No equilibrium at κ = 0: |N_Ed| exceeds the axial force capacity (N_Rd compression = {{druk}} kN, tension = {{trek}} kN).

memberWindow.notRecognised: this member was not recognised as a concrete member
memberWindow.orientationStanding: vertical, checked from base to top: in the drawing left = base; bottom = right-hand side, top = left-hand side
memberWindow.toGoverningTitle: Move the cursor to the location the calculation engine identified as governing — the highest unity check outside the end zones.
memberWindow.noLength: This member has no length; there is nothing to draw.
memberWindow.classesNotLoaded: Concrete classes not loaded from the calculation engine (the static list is used): {{fout}}
memberWindow.clickToPick: Click in the elevation to pick a section
memberWindow.sectionUnreadable: The cross-section cannot be read from the section name “{{profiel}}”; enter it in the member properties.
memberWindow.endZoneTitle: Within l_bd of a bar end §9.2.1.4/§9.2.1.5 applies, not the free coverage line; the engine excludes this part when identifying the governing location.
memberWindow.noCoverLineYet: No coverage line yet — the reason is given in the messages below the drawing.
memberWindow.notCalculated: No calculation has been run yet. The coverage line comes from the calculation engine and needs the force distribution of the ULS combinations; press Calculate.
memberWindow.engineUnreachable: The last calculation run did not reach the calculation engine, so there is no coverage line. Pressing Calculate again will not change that. The engine reported:
memberWindow.browserBridge: This view is running in a browser: the coverage line comes from the Rust calculation engine, which can only be reached here via the dev bridge of the development server. Without that bridge it only works in the desktop app.
memberWindow.zonesChanged: The zone layout has just been changed. The drawing still shows the previous calculation — the zone boundaries are calculation nodes, so the line is waiting for the new force distribution.
memberWindow.missedBoundary: At {{plaatsen}} there is a zone boundary without a calculation node. There the required force from an adjacent station is set against the resistance at this point; the step is not reliable at that location.
memberWindow.crackBusy: The crack width is requested from the calculation engine per section (§7.3.4 is not a line but a cross-section check); this takes a moment.
memberWindow.crackSummary: Crack width — {{aantal}} of {{totaal}} sections returned a w_k
memberWindow.notesSummary: Notes from the calculation engine ({{aantal}}) — a_l = {{al}} mm according to {{artikel}}
memberWindow.supportNoteBegin: Support at start (x = {{x}} mm): A_s required {{vereist}} mm², provided {{aanwezig}} mm², F_Ed = {{fed}} kN, l_bd = {{lbd}} — {{eis}}.
memberWindow.supportNoteEnd: Support at end (x = {{x}} mm): A_s required {{vereist}} mm², provided {{aanwezig}} mm², F_Ed = {{fed}} kN, l_bd = {{lbd}} — {{eis}}.
memberWindow.areaNotMet: the area requirement is NOT met

zones.shapeStraightHint: Straight bar ends — α₁ = 1.0 in table 8.2.
zones.shapeBentHint: Bend, hook or loop. Table 8.2 gives α₁ = 0.7 for c_d > 3Φ; if c_d is not given, α₁ stays 1.0 and the bend therefore does not shorten l_bd.
zones.noZonesHint: This member has no reinforcement zones yet: the cage applies over the full length, so the resistance line is straight. Add zones to curtail the longitudinal reinforcement (§9.2.1.3) or to tighten the stirrups near the supports (§9.2.2).
zones.createTitle: Places one zone per side over the full length. This calculates exactly as now; only splitting and removing bars changes anything.
zones.splitTitle: Split this zone in two. Both halves keep the same bars; then reduce the number in one of them.
zones.splitTitleAt: Split this zone in two at x = {{x}} mm. Both halves keep the same bars; then reduce the number in one of them.
zones.splitStirrupTitle: Split this stirrup zone in two.
zones.splitStirrupTitleAt: Split this stirrup zone in two at x = {{x}} mm.
zones.removeTitle: Remove all zones; the member's cage then applies over the full length again.
zones.countTitle: Number of bars in this part. Zero is valid: it means there is no longitudinal reinforcement on this side here.
zones.castingTitle: Figure 8.2 — determines η₁ in (8.2). The same beam cast from above or precast on its side differs in l_bd by a factor of 1.43; the model cannot derive this.
zones.mergeTitle: Extend this zone over its right-hand neighbour; the reinforcement of THIS zone remains in force.
zones.stirrupToggleTitle: Switch stirrup zones on or off. Without stirrup zones the stirrup fields of the cage apply over the full length.
zones.noStirrupZonesHint: No stirrup zones: the stirrup fields of the cage apply over the full length. That is allowed — §6.2.1(4) does require minimum reinforcement everywhere, but an EMPTY list here means "nothing special", not "no stirrups".
zones.spacingTitle: Centre-to-centre spacing along the longitudinal axis — symbol s in (9.4), limited by s_l,max in §9.2.2(6).
zones.legsTitle: Number of stirrup legs crossing one vertical section — §9.2.2(5).
zones.mergeStirrupTitle: Extend this stirrup zone over its right-hand neighbour.

elevation.ariaLabel: Elevation of the concrete member over {{lengte}} m with the coverage lines
elevation.anchorage: Anchorage length l_bd = {{lbd}} mm: the bar does not yet develop its full force here (§9.2.1.3(3))
elevation.noTension: {{label}} is zero everywhere: there is no tension on this side
elevation.noUcPerSection: No unity check per section available.
elevation.xAxis: x [m] from the left (vertical member: from the base)

column.braced: Braced — does NOT contribute to horizontal stability
column.unbraced: Unbraced (bracing member) — DOES contribute to stability
column.bracingHint: Braced or unbraced is a design decision (cl. 5.8.1) and is not derived from the model: a frame with wind bracing looks no different here from the same frame without it. Without this choice the slenderness limit of 5.8.3.1 remains unchecked, with that reason stated in the report.
column.verticalHint: This member is almost vertical; if it carries axial compression, 5.8 applies to it.
column.l0Info: l₀ = {{l0}} m for a clear length l = {{l}} m.
column.casesFgHint: Cases f) and g) of figure 5.7 — partial fixity — are not listed: they require the relative flexibility k = (θ/M)·(EI/l) of each member end, which cannot be read from a frame model. Work out (5.15) or (5.16) yourself and then choose "enter l₀ manually".
column.phiHint: Final value of the creep coefficient according to cl. 3.1.4. Empty = not specified, and then the project value of φ(∞,t₀) applies; if that is empty but ‘annex B’ is ticked, the value calculated according to annex B applies (from the relative humidity, h₀ of the cross-section, the cement class and t₀). If that is missing too, φ_ef remains unknown: 5.8.3.1(1) then uses A = 0.7 — not the safe side but the value for φ_ef ≈ 2.14 — and about the z-axis the moment is not approved while e₂ counts (5.8.4(1)P). If φ(∞,t₀) is known but the quasi-permanent combination is missing, φ(∞,t₀) is used as an upper bound of φ_ef.
column.zAxisHeader: About the z-axis (perpendicular to the plane) — cl. 5.8.9
column.zAxisHint: The frame solver calculates in one plane and gives M_z = 0, but a column also buckles about the z-axis: the imperfection of cl. 5.2 (θ₀ = 1/300, national annex) and the second-order effect in that direction do not depend on the model. The engine therefore always calculates M_Ed,z = M₀Ed,z + N_Ed·(e_i + e₂), checks it against M_Rd,z with the bars in their positions across the width, and then verifies cl. 5.8.9: may the directions be treated separately ((5.38a) and (5.38b)), and if not, the interaction (5.39). The bracing and buckling length about z are SEPARATE inputs — a column can be braced in the plane and unbraced perpendicular to it; empty = the choice for the plane is adopted, with that note in the report. M₀Ed,z external is a first-order moment about z from a spatial model or a hand calculation; 0 = none.
column.stirrupZoneNotGiven: — not specified, s_cl,tmax is not checked —
column.stirrupZoneNearLap: Near a lap splice with Ø > 14 mm — 9.5.3(4)ii, ×0.6
column.lapsNotGiven: — not specified, A_s,max is not checked —
column.lapsElsewhere: Laps elsewhere in the column — A_s,max = 0.04·A_c
column.choicesHint: These two choices belong to cl. 9.5. They are not assumed: the regular stirrup zone and "no laps" are both the MOST LENIENT branch, and silently adopting them could approve too large a stirrup spacing or too heavy reinforcement. If they remain empty, s_cl,tmax and A_s,max appear in the report as not performed, with the reason.
column.detailingHint: Cl. 9.5.2(4) (a bar in every corner) and 9.5.3(6) (every corner bar restrained, no bar further than 150 mm from a restrained bar) are checked using the position of every bar in the cage — including the side bars. A_s in ω and in 9.5.2 is the TOTAL longitudinal reinforcement.

mk.ariaLabel: M-κ diagram at N = {{n}} kN; M_Rd = {{mrd}} kNm at κ = {{kappa}} per thousand metres

interaction.ariaLabel: N-M interaction diagram; {{aantal}} points on the failure envelope
interaction.ariaLabelWithPoint: N-M interaction diagram; {{aantal}} points on the failure envelope, design point N = {{n}} kN and M = {{m}} kNm
interaction.momentAxis: moment M [kNm] — positive: tension at bottom

ei.ariaLabel: Flexural stiffness EI along the member; uncracked E_c·I_c = {{ei}} kNm²

moment.label: Moment coverage
moment.hint: §9.2.1.3, figure 9.2 — the required tensile force F_s (after the shift a_l) next to the resisting force F_Rs of the bars actually present, per side

dwarskracht.label: Shear coverage
dwarskracht.hint: §6.2 — |V_Ed| next to V_Rd per section, with the route that gave V_Rd; V_Rd,c and V_Rd,s are never added together

scheurwijdte.label: Crack width
scheurwijdte.hint: §7.3.4 — w_k per section under the frequent SLS combination, next to w_max from table 7.1N; requested per section from the calculation engine and therefore off by default

uc.label: Unity checks
uc.hint: The governing unity check per section over the other three layers, as a colour bar — green ≤ 0.9, amber up to 1.0, red above

cageCheck.webWidthPositive: The web width b_w must be positive.
cageCheck.flangeThicknessPositive: The flange thickness h_f must be positive.
cageCheck.webNarrowerThanFlange: The web width b_w must be smaller than the flange width b_f.
cageCheck.flangeLeavesNoWeb: The flange thickness h_f leaves no web within the height h.
cageCheck.coverNegative: Cover and stirrup diameter must not be negative.
cageCheck.sideCoverInvalid: The cover on the {{zijde}} is {{waarde}} mm; that is not a dimension. Leave the field empty if this side follows the cover of the element.
cageCheck.noMainBars: The cage contains no main reinforcement.
cageCheck.onlySideBars: The cage only has side bars and no top or bottom reinforcement.
cageCheck.sideBarsNoDiameter: {{aantal}} side bars per side are specified without a diameter; choose a bar diameter or set the number to 0.
cageCheck.rowWidthAtHeight: (the section is {{breedte}} mm wide at z = {{z}} mm)
cageCheck.rowTooWide: {{naam}} {{rij}} does not fit in the width: {{staal}} mm of steel in {{binnenmaat}} mm clear width{{waar}}.
cageCheck.topBottomOverlap: Top and bottom reinforcement overlap in height.
cageCheck.sideBarsWidth: The side bars {{rij}} per side do not fit next to each other: their centres are {{afstand}} mm apart while Ø{{diameter}} mm is needed.
cageCheck.sideBarsHeight: The side bars {{rij}} per side do not fit in the height: they end up {{steek}} mm apart, less than their own Ø{{diameter}} mm.
cageCheck.stirrupSpacingPositive: The stirrup spacing s must be greater than zero; leave the field empty if it is not specified.
cageCheck.legSpacingPositive: The transverse spacing of the stirrup legs must be greater than zero; leave the field empty if it is not specified.
cageCheck.fywkPositive: The yield strength f_ywk of the stirrups must be greater than zero; leave the field empty if it is not specified.
cageCheck.legsMin1: The number of stirrup legs must be at least 1; leave the field empty if there are no stirrups.
cageCheck.stirrupDataWithoutStirrup: Stirrup data are specified while there is no stirrup; choose a stirrup diameter or leave the stirrup data empty.
cageCheck.legSpacingTooLarge: The transverse spacing of the stirrup legs is {{afstand}} mm, but at most {{ruimte}} mm fits between the outer leg axes.

zoneCheck.zeroLength: The member length is zero; without a length there is no zone layout.
zoneCheck.notANumber: {{aanduiding}}: the start or end dimension is not a number.
zoneCheck.endBeforeStart: {{aanduiding}}: the end ({{eind}} mm) does not lie beyond the start ({{begin}} mm).
zoneCheck.outsideMember: {{aanduiding}}: {{begin}}…{{eind}} mm lies outside the member from 0 to {{lengte}} mm.
zoneCheck.stirrupZoneIncomplete: The stirrup zone {{begin}}…{{eind}} mm is incomplete: s, Ø and the number of legs must all three be filled in.
zoneCheck.cageDoesNotFitAt: At x = {{x}} mm the reinforcement does not fit: {{fout}}
zoneCheck.firstZoneNotAtZero: For {{reeks}} the first zone starts at {{begin}} mm; it must start at 0 mm.
zoneCheck.gap: For {{reeks}} there is a gap of {{gat}} mm between {{van}} and {{tot}} mm. A length without reinforcement is a zone with zero bars, not a gap.
zoneCheck.overlap: For {{reeks}} two zones overlap between {{van}} and {{tot}} mm.
zoneCheck.lastZoneShort: For {{reeks}} the last zone ends at {{eind}} mm; it must continue to {{lengte}} mm.

beam.title: Member {{id}}
beam.timberLcrzHint: For timber, L_cr,z also enters the compression term of the lateral-torsional buckling check (6.35).
beam.bracingPositions: At {{posities}} m from the start node.
beam.standingTop: Vertical member, checked from base to head: top is the LEFT side here, as the member stands in the model.
beam.standingBottom: Vertical member, checked from base to head: bottom is the RIGHT side here, as the member stands in the model.
beam.bracingFillHint: Enter a number for equal spacing, or type fractions yourself (0–1).
beam.ltbSpacingHint: Empty = member length ({{lengte}} m). This is the ℓ from which table 6.1 derives the effective length l_ef (l_ef = 0.9·ℓ for a uniformly distributed load on two supports); l_ef determines σ_m,crit and hence k_crit.
beam.ltbOffHint: LTB check off: you declare that the compression edge is laterally restrained over its full length (roof sheathing, floor slab) and that the supports are torsionally restrained, so k_crit = 1.0 (cl. 6.3.3(5)). This assumption is stated as such in the report.
beam.kCrHint: b_ef = k_cr · b (6.13a). Empty = 1.0: NEN-EN 1995-1-1/NB at 6.1.7 for a prismatic cross-section. The European recommendation of 6.1.7(2) is 0.67 for solid and glued laminated timber; only values in (0, 1] are stored.
beam.climateHint: Service class: k_mod and k_def. Automatic load duration: k_mod per ULS combination from the shortest-duration load (EN 1995-1-1 3.1.3(2)); a chosen class acts as a lower bound.
beam.noCageHint: Without a cage the member is not checked; the check panel then states this with the reason.
beam.standingConcreteHint: Vertical member, checked from base to head: the BOTTOM reinforcement lies on the RIGHT and the TOP reinforcement on the LEFT, as the member stands in the model. A positive moment gives tension on the right.
beam.loadRoleTitle:
Determines which load plane this member carries.
Facade and roof receive wind load; floor and interior member do not.
beam.loadRoleManual: Set manually — the wind generator uses this member type.
beam.loadRoleDerived: Follows from the geometry ({{hoek}}° from horizontal). Choose a member type yourself to fix it.
beam.taperHint: The dimensions vary linearly along the member. The solver divides it into segments for this; the check evaluates every cross-section check at each calculation point with the cross-section actually present there.
beam.chooseProfileTitle: Choose section and material in one step (wizard)

load.title: Load {{id}}
load.descriptionTitle: Free name for this load; appears in the load table of the report and does not change the calculation.
load.edgePositionTitle: Distance along the edge from the start corner (corner i for an edge index; the smallest x or z for a named edge).
load.coordSystemTitle:
Global: the load acts in world axes (vertical/horizontal), regardless of the member slope.
Local: the load rotates with the member (perpendicular to or along the member axis).
q is always per metre of member length.
load.directionLocalTitle: Local z: perpendicular to the member axis. Local x: axial along the member.
load.directionGlobalTitle: World Z: vertical (negative = downward). World X: horizontal (wind).
load.startTitleBeam: Distance from the start node (0 – {{lengte}} m); 0 to {{lengte}} = full length
load.endTitleBeam: Distance from the start node (0 – {{lengte}} m)
load.startTitleEdge: Distance from the start corner of the edge (0 – {{lengte}} m); 0 to {{lengte}} = the full edge
load.endTitleEdge: Distance from the start corner of the edge (0 – {{lengte}} m)
load.edgeDirectionTitle:
World Z: vertical (negative = downward). World X: horizontal.
p is per metre of edge length.

plate.title: Plate {{id}}
plate.materialPlaceholder: empty = own E, ν and ρ
plate.materialTitleAttr: Steel grade (S235–S460), concrete class (C20/25…), timber strength class (C24, GL28h…), cross-laminated timber ("CLT C24 40/20/40/20/40") or a free material ("VRIJ:NaturalStone E=60000 rho=2700 f=8"). Leave empty = calculate with the separate E, ν and ρ below, as before.
plate.materialRejectedHint: As long as this is not correct, the calculation refuses with the same message.
plate.mainDirectionTitle: Counter-clockwise angle from the global x axis to direction 1: the grain direction; for cross-laminated timber the direction of the longitudinal layers. Empty or 0 = horizontal.
plate.orthotropic: Orthotropic: E₁ = {{e1}} N/mm² in direction 1, E₂ = {{e2}} N/mm² perpendicular to it, G₁₂ = {{g12}} N/mm², ν₁₂ = {{nu12}}.
plate.cltG12Title: In-plane shear modulus of this cross-laminated timber plate, from the product declaration or the ETA. EN 1995-1-1 and EN 338 do not give it for a crosswise lay-up; no value is assumed. Required together with the source.
plate.cltG12SourceTitle: Where G₁₂ comes from. Without a source the value is rejected: otherwise the report cannot tell it apart from an assumption.
plate.cltG12UpperBoundTitle: Deliberately use the smeared G_mean of the lamellae, without reduction for the crossing areas. This is an upper bound: the plate is too stiff in shear. The report carries a warning.
plate.thicknessTitle: Plate thickness t — stresses scale inversely (t ×2 → σ ×0.5)
plate.eOverrideTitle: Overrides the material's E, in BOTH directions — the plate is then calculated as isotropic. Leave empty = follow the material's value.
plate.nuOverrideTitle: Overrides the material's ν₁₂. Leave empty = follow the material's value.
plate.rhoOverrideTitle: Overrides the material's ρ, and with it the self-weight ρ·t·A. Leave empty = follow the material's value.
plate.rhoTitle: Density — used for the self-weight (steel 7850, concrete 2500)
plate.meshSizeTitle: Desired element size of the calculation mesh; smaller = more accurate but heavier (limit ±4000 degrees of freedom)
plate.elementsTitle: Quadrilaterals (Quad4, bilinear) are more accurate per degree of freedom than triangles (CST, constant strain); triangles need a finer mesh. Default = the choice from before September 2026 for this shape.
plate.meshMixed: Mixed: quadrilaterals where pairing succeeds, triangles elsewhere
plate.noOpeningsAfter: in the ribbon and drag a rectangle inside the plate.
plate.openingsHint: The calculation mesh leaves the openings free and places nodes on the opening edge.
plate.openingsHintCdt: A non-rectangular opening is calculated via the CDT (mesh cache).
plate.serviceClassTitle: Service class for the plate check (NEN-EN 1995-1-1 2.3.1.3): together with the load duration it sets k_mod. The stiffness does not change.

wapening.fctHint: f_ct,eff at expected cracking; not automatically inferred from the concrete class.
wapening.scheurGrens: Crack width: frequent SLS, uniaxial membrane tension, symmetric layers, Ø ≥ 5 mm, c ≥ max(Ø;10 mm) and s ≤ 5(c+Ø/2). Full nominal cover, shrinkage, anchorage and out-of-plane effects remain unchecked. Missing basis = no crack check.
wapening.hint: Provided reinforcement for the plate check (EN 1992-1-1 annex F, 9.6, 7.3); the stiffness does not change.
wapening.milieuklasseHint: Exposure class (table 4.1): the entry of table 7.1N for w_max. Empty = crack width not checked.

barDialog.title: Member properties #{{id}}
barDialog.unsaved: Not saved yet — confirm with OK
barDialog.chooseProfileTitle: Choose section and material in one step (wizard)
barDialog.connectionsHint: Per end N, V and M: fixed, hinge (released) or spring with stiffness — N and V in kN/mm, M in kNm/rad.
barDialog.foundationToggle: Elastically supported over the full length (Winkler)
barDialog.foundationIncomplete: Enter k and b greater than zero; otherwise no elastic foundation is applied.
barDialog.foundationHint: Line stiffness k·b; the member is automatically subdivided finely enough at 1/λ = (4EI/(k·b))^¼.
barDialog.sigmaZHint: Transverse stress perpendicular to the member axis, for example a bearing pressure. A beam element does not compute it itself. Empty or 0 leaves σ_eq = √(σ_x² + 3τ²).
barDialog.governingLine: Governing: {{toets}} — UC {{uc}}. Full derivation: Check tab → check panel.
barDialog.notChecked: Not checked yet — run the code check via the ribbon tab "Check" (button "Check steel + timber").

plaat.krachtregel: Combination {{combinatie}} — element-averaged in-plane stresses; the element is named in the notes
plaat.wapening: Required reinforcement (annex F): x up to {{x}} kN/m (element {{ex}}), z up to {{z}} kN/m (element {{ez}}) — provided reinforcement not checked
